```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## What this notebook does

This notebook checks the main numbers in the women on boards story. The only thing it takes from Claude is the list of numbers being checked. It:

1. downloads the raw data directly from EIGE (the European Institute for Gender Equality) onto your Mac,
2. works out each number from scratch, and
3. prints each number next to the number in the story, with a **match** column.

If the story's numbers had been made up rather than calculated, they wouldn't match.

**Before you start:** if you haven't already, run `install.packages("tidyverse")` once in the RStudio console. Then press **Knit**.

**Where the downloads go:** `~/Desktop/Claude-checker/women-on-boards/raw-data`. It's only downloaded the first time.

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
```

## Step 1: download the raw file

This is the same EIGE export as the one in the story's data folder: largest listed companies, all sectors, headcounts and percentages, every position.

```{r download}
raw_dir <- path.expand("~/Desktop/Claude-checker/women-on-boards/raw-data")
dir.create(raw_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
options(timeout = 600)

url  <- paste0("https://eige.europa.eu/gender-statistics/dgs/export/indicator/",
               "wmidm_bus_bus__wmid_comp_compbm/bar/csv/",
               "EGROUP:COMP/sex:M,T,W/UNIT:NR,PC/",
               "POSITION:PRES_BRD,MEMB_BRD,CEO,EXEC,NON_EXEC,NON_EXEC_EXER,EMP_REP/NACE:TOT")
dest <- file.path(raw_dir, "eige_wmid_comp.csv")
if (!file.exists(dest)) download.file(url, dest, mode = "wb")

raw <- read_csv(dest, show_col_types = FALSE)
nrow(raw)   # 48,552 rows on 22 October 2026; more if EIGE has added a half-year since
```

## Step 2: compute the numbers

```{r compute}
# Headcounts only (not EIGE's percentages): one row per country, period, position,
# with columns women and total
nr <- raw |>
  filter(`_UNIT` == "NR", `_sex` %in% c("W", "T")) |>
  select(geo = `_geo`, time, pos = `_POSITION`, sex = `_sex`, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = sex, values_from = value) |>
  rename(women = W, total = T)

# The 30 countries compared: EU27, Norway, Iceland and the UK
# (EU totals and the candidate countries are left out)
not_compared <- c("EU27_2020", "EEA", "IPA", "TR", "RS", "ME", "MK", "BA")
quota        <- c("NO", "IS", "FR", "IT", "BE", "DE", "AT", "PT")
countries    <- setdiff(unique(nr$geo), not_compared)

nr <- nr |>
  mutate(group = case_when(geo == "UK"       ~ "UK",
                           geo %in% quota    ~ "Quota",
                           geo %in% countries ~ "No quota"))

# Excel-style rounding (R's round() rounds 0.5 to the even number)
round_up <- function(x, d = 0) floor(x * 10^d + 0.5 + 1e-9) / 10^d

# Women's share for a group, pooled by headcount: all women / all people
group_share <- function(g, p, t) {
  nr |> filter(group == g, pos == p, time == t) |>
    summarise(s = 100 * sum(women) / sum(total)) |> pull(s)
}
# Women's share for one country (or the EU27 total)
geo_share <- function(g, p, t) {
  nr |> filter(geo == g, pos == p, time == t) |> mutate(s = 100 * women / total) |> pull(s)
}
geo_count <- function(g, p, t, which) {
  nr |> filter(geo == g, pos == p, time == t) |> pull({{ which }})
}
group_count <- function(g, p, t, which) {
  nr |> filter(group == g, pos == p, time == t) |> summarise(n = sum({{ which }})) |> pull(n)
}

end <- "2024-B2"; start <- "2012-B2"

q_exec  <- group_share("Quota", "EXEC", end)
nq_exec <- group_share("No quota", "EXEC", end)

# Every country's executive share in both years, for the UK ranking claims
by_country <- nr |>
  filter(geo %in% countries, pos %in% c("EXEC", "NON_EXEC"), time %in% c(start, end)) |>
  mutate(s = 100 * women / total) |>
  select(geo, time, pos, s) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(pos, time), values_from = s) |>
  mutate(rise = `EXEC_2024-B2` - `EXEC_2012-B2`)

uk_ceo_t <- geo_count("UK", "CEO", end, total)
eu_ceo_t <- geo_count("EU27_2020", "CEO", end, total)
eu_ceo_w <- geo_count("EU27_2020", "CEO", end, women)
eu_ned   <- geo_share("EU27_2020", "NON_EXEC", end)
eu_match <- round_up(eu_ceo_t * eu_ned / 100)

# EIGE's own percentages against our recomputed ones
pct_gap <- raw |>
  filter(`_UNIT` == "PC", `_sex` == "W", `_geo` %in% countries,
         `_POSITION` %in% c("NON_EXEC", "EXEC", "CEO"), time >= start, time <= end) |>
  select(geo = `_geo`, time, pos = `_POSITION`, eige = value) |>
  inner_join(nr, by = c("geo", "time", "pos")) |>
  filter(total > 0) |>
  summarise(m = max(abs(100 * women / total - eige))) |> pull(m)
```

## Step 3: compare with the story

```{r compare}
story <- tribble(
  ~claim,                                            ~in_story, ~in_r,                                               ~dp,
  "Quota countries, % of executive jobs",            25.3,  q_exec,                                                  1,
  "Rest of Europe, % of executive jobs",             23.1,  nq_exec,                                                 1,
  "Gap, points",                                     2,     q_exec - nq_exec,                                        0,
  "Quota countries, % of non-executive seats",       43.8,  group_share("Quota", "NON_EXEC", end),                   1,
  "Rest of Europe, % of non-executive seats",        32.6,  group_share("No quota", "NON_EXEC", end),                1,
  "Quota countries, women CEOs",                     19,    group_count("Quota", "CEO", end, women),                     0,
  "Quota countries, companies",                      211,   group_count("Quota", "CEO", end, total),                     0,
  "Rest of Europe, women CEOs",                      38,    group_count("No quota", "CEO", end, women),                  0,
  "Rest of Europe, companies",                       398,   group_count("No quota", "CEO", end, total),                  0,
  "Quota exec share, rise since 2012, points",       17,    q_exec - group_share("Quota", "EXEC", start),            0,
  "Rest of Europe exec share, rise, points",         11,    nq_exec - group_share("No quota", "EXEC", start),        0,
  "Quota, non-exec minus exec gap, 2012",            11,    group_share("Quota", "NON_EXEC", start) - group_share("Quota", "EXEC", start), 0,
  "Quota, non-exec minus exec gap, 2024",            18,    group_share("Quota", "NON_EXEC", end) - q_exec,          0,
  "Italy, % of non-executive seats",                 50.0,  geo_share("IT", "NON_EXEC", end),                        1,
  "Italy, % of executive jobs",                      17.0,  geo_share("IT", "EXEC", end),                            1,
  "Italy, % of executive jobs, 2012",                4.3,   geo_share("IT", "EXEC", start),                          1,
  "Italy, women CEOs",                               1,     geo_count("IT", "CEO", end, women),                          0,
  "Italy, companies",                                35,    geo_count("IT", "CEO", end, total),                          0,
  "UK, % of executive jobs",                         34.5,  geo_share("UK", "EXEC", end),                            1,
  "UK, % of executive jobs, 2012",                   11.0,  geo_share("UK", "EXEC", start),                          1,
  "UK has the highest exec share (1 = yes)",         1,     as.numeric(by_country$geo[which.max(by_country$`EXEC_2024-B2`)] == "UK"), 0,
  "UK has the largest rise (1 = yes)",               1,     as.numeric(by_country$geo[which.max(by_country$rise)] == "UK"), 0,
  "Countries compared",                              30,    length(countries),                                       0,
  "UK, % of non-executive seats",                    49.7,  geo_share("UK", "NON_EXEC", end),                        1,
  "France, % of non-executive seats",                49.9,  geo_share("FR", "NON_EXEC", end),                        1,
  "UK, women CEOs",                                  7,     geo_count("UK", "CEO", end, women),                          0,
  "UK, companies",                                   48,    uk_ceo_t,                                                0,
  "UK, CEOs if they matched non-exec share",         24,    uk_ceo_t * geo_share("UK", "NON_EXEC", end) / 100,       0,
  "EU, women CEOs",                                  49,    eu_ceo_w,                                                0,
  "EU, companies",                                   563,   eu_ceo_t,                                                0,
  "EU, % of non-executive seats",                    37.2,  eu_ned,                                                  1,
  "EU, CEOs if they matched non-exec share",         209,   eu_match,                                                0,
  "EU, missing women CEOs",                          160,   eu_match - eu_ceo_w,                                     0,
  "Countries where non-exec share > exec share",     25,    sum(by_country$`NON_EXEC_2024-B2` > by_country$`EXEC_2024-B2`), 0
)

story |>
  mutate(in_r = round_up(in_r, dp),
         match = if_else(abs(in_story - in_r) < 0.0005, "match", "CHECK")) |>
  select(-dp) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

**One more check:** the largest gap between EIGE's own percentages and the shares worked out from headcounts is `r round(pct_gap, 3)` points. The story says "within 0.05 points".

**Not checked here:** the UK review figures (Davies, Hampton-Alexander, FTSE Women Leaders) and the law dates. They come from the reports, not from EIGE, and are listed with page numbers on the *Report figures* sheet of the check workbook.
